technical illustration · iso kit gallery

Teardowns

Exploded views after the teardown skill: each figure is drawn taken apart along its assembly paths. Use Exploded and Assembled or the Spread slider to put it together, and point at a part to name it.

Teardown of an interface card

The teardown skill's own concept example: an interface card taken apart into page, card surface, media, text and the primary button. Switch to Assembled to stack the layers back, or drag the Spread slider; point at a layer to name it.

Teardown of a hard drive

After teardown's Drive: the circuit board drops below the base casting, the spindle motor, three platters and the disc clamp rise up the spindle, the head stack swings aside and the top cover lifts clear. Assembled closes the cover over all of it.

Teardown of a CPU in its socket

After teardown's CPU: motherboard and chokes, the socket frame and its pin field, the package substrate with capacitors, the die, thermal paste, the heat spreader and the retention lid with its lever, stacked along one axis.

Teardown of a graphics card

After teardown's GPU: backplate, board with GPU, memory, power stages and display ports, the I/O bracket pulled out sideways, the cold plate, two heat pipes, a sixty-fin stack and the shroud with three fans.

Teardown of display pixels

The teardown skill's concept of layered pixels: backlight, rear polariser, transistor grid, liquid crystal, black matrix, the red, green and blue filters and the cover glass, each lifted off the one below.
